facts.headline: The tower everyone calls "Big Ben" isn't actually named that
facts.body_html: "Big Ben" is the nickname of the 13.5-tonne bell hanging inside the clock tower at the Palace of Westminster — the tower itself is officially the Elizabeth Tower, renamed in 2012 for the Queen's Diamond Jubilee.
suggested_queries: Elizabeth Tower Big Ben London clock face
Palace of Westminster clock tower exterior

facts.headline: Legend says the kingdom falls the day these six birds leave
facts.body_html: Since Charles II's reign, the Tower of London has kept at least six ravens on site, guarding against an old legend that if they ever leave, the Crown itself will fall. Their wings are still clipped today, just in case.
suggested_queries: Tower of London ravens Yeoman Ravenmaster
Tower of London raven close up

facts.headline: Buckingham Palace has more rooms than most hotels
facts.body_html: The Palace contains 775 rooms in total — including 92 offices, 78 bathrooms, and 188 staff bedrooms — making it one of the largest working royal residences still in use anywhere on Earth.

facts.headline: The world's first underground railway opened here in 1863
facts.body_html: The Metropolitan Railway between Paddington and Farringdon became the world's first underground passenger railway, running steam locomotives through smoke-filled tunnels more than 160 years ago.

Baker Street tube station platform old

facts.headline: A Victorian time capsule has sat buried under this obelisk since 1878
facts.body_html: Beneath Cleopatra's Needle on the Victoria Embankment sits a sealed time capsule from 1878, packed with items like a box of cigars, a baby's bottle, and photographs of a dozen "pretty Englishwomen" of the day.

facts.headline: A tiny park hides ceramic tributes to strangers who died saving strangers
facts.body_html: Tucked inside Postman's Park, the Memorial to Heroic Self-Sacrifice holds dozens of Victorian ceramic tablets, each honoring an ordinary Londoner who died saving someone else's life.
suggested_queries: Postman's Park Memorial Heroic Self-Sacrifice tiles

facts.headline: Knights Templar effigies still lie inside this 800-year-old church
facts.body_html: Built by the Knights Templar in the 12th century, Temple Church still holds stone effigies of medieval knights on its floor — and later inspired a key scene in The Da Vinci Code.
